title: The scientometrics and reciprocality underlying co-authorship panels in Google Scholar profiles
short_title: Scientometrics and reciprocality in Google Scholar co-author panels

affiliations.2: Department of Mathematics, Ariel University, Ariel, Israel

abstract: Online academic profiles are used by scholars to reflect a desired image to their online audience. In Google Scholar, scholars can select a subset of co-authors for presentation in a central location on their profile using a social feature called the “co-authroship panel”. In this work, we examine whether scientometrics and reciprocality can explain the observed selections. To this end, we scrape and thoroughly analyze a novel set of 120,000 Google Scholar profiles, ranging across four dieffectsciplines and various academic institutions. Our results seem to suggest that scholars tend to favor co-authors with higher scientometrics over others for inclusion in their co-authorship panels. Interestingly, as one’s own scientometrics are higher, the tendency to include co-authors with high scientometrics is diminishing. Furthermore, we find that reciprocality is central in explaining scholars’ selections.
summary: Google Scholar lets scholars showcase a chosen subset of their co-authors in a co-authorship panel on their profile. We asked whether research-impact metrics (scientometrics) and reciprocity explain these choices, by collecting and analyzing a new set of 120,000 Google Scholar profiles across four disciplines and various institutions. Scholars tended to favor co-authors with higher scientometrics, this tendency weakened as their own scientometrics rose, and reciprocity was central to explaining their selections.
key_findings: We scraped and analyzed a novel set of 120,000 Google Scholar profiles spanning four disciplines and various academic institutions.
Scholars tend to favor co-authors with higher scientometrics for inclusion in their co-authorship panels.
The higher a scholar's own scientometrics, the weaker the tendency to include co-authors with high scientometrics.
Reciprocality is central in explaining which co-authors scholars select.
